A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SpatialLM and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–D. Content can be matched reliably despite section reordering and figure renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original encoder and training experiments, Structured3D and ScanNet evaluations, and appendix results for video inputs and semantic label completion.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and appendix outcomes, with revised numerical results for layout estimation.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same Sonata/PTv3 encoder, two-layer MLP, Qwen2.5-0.5B backbone, structured text outputs, and training procedures. The new encoder diagram documents the existing five-level architecture; no procedural change is stated.

E1.justification: Both use the SpatialLM dataset, Structured3D, ScanNet, and 107 virtual room-tour videos. Appendix D retains the same generated, real-video, MultiScan, and HSSD input scenarios, category-conditioned detection, and semantic label completion.

E2.justification: Layout comparisons retain RoomFormer and SceneScript; object-detection comparisons retain V-DETR and SceneScript. Table 2 also retains the same six encoder alternatives. Added parameter counts do not change comparator membership.

E3.justification: The reported splits, IoU thresholds, F1 metrics, resolution sweep, training schedules, augmentations, and training budgets remain unchanged, including Appendix B and Table 8. No protocol revision is stated to explain the changed layout scores.

E4.justification: Tables 2–4 revise the layout evidence within the existing encoder, resolution, and training-schedule analyses. In Table 4, the two-stage variant becomes best at both layout thresholds, whereas v1 favored single-stage training at IoU 0.25. The analysis designs and appendix robustness demonstrations remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report performance point estimates without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting procedure is added or revised.

E6.justification: Layout scores are substantially revised across Tables 2–5, 9, and 12. Structured3D F1 at IoU 0.25/0.5 changes from 86.5/84.6 to 94.3/93.5 for the final SpatialLM model, 70.4/67.2 to 83.4/81.4 for RoomFormer, and 83.1/80.8 to 90.4/89.2 for SceneScript. Video-layout F1 changes from 52.9 to 55.7. Object-detection scores remain unchanged. The PDFs do not explain the numerical revisions, so they do not establish an improved model.

T1.justification: The structured representations, encoder mapping in Equation 1, and mathematical descriptions of matching and evaluation are retained. Neither version introduces theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: structured modeling through an LLM, a large synthetic dataset, an empirical alignment study, state-of-the-art layout estimation, and competitive object detection. Revised scores do not change these claims.

C2.justification: The explanations of encoder performance, resolution, training schedules, dataset benefits, and video reconstruction remain substantively unchanged. Both retain the same limitations concerning generalization, untested language capabilities, and predefined categories. No interpretation of the score revisions is added.

D1.justification: v2 adds parameter counts in Tables 2, 5, and 6, identifies Kujiale as the dataset source platform, and supplies encoder stage widths, block counts, and pooling details in new Figure 11. Existing hyperparameters, hardware, training time, augmentation settings, and prompts are retained.

R1.justification: The same 68 references are retained. v2 modestly sharpens the explicit distinction from SceneScript and other 3D language models, and removes the description of RoomFormer as a two-stage network. Research positioning otherwise remains stable.

P1.justification: Related Work moves from Section 4 to Section 2; the empirical-method section becomes SpatialLM, and the benchmark section becomes Experiments. There are limited explanatory and grammatical edits and an updated conference footer, while most prose and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the encoder-hierarchy diagram as Figure 11 and parameter-count columns to Tables 2, 5, and 6. Existing figures are relocated or resized, and subsequent appendix figures are renumbered. The existing qualitative imagery and dataset visualizations are retained.

improvement.justification: Parameter counts, the encoder diagram, and source attribution provide a limited improvement in transparency and implementation clarity. The unexplained layout-score revisions cannot themselves be credited as better performance. The retained claim favoring single-stage training also fits Table 4 less well now that two-stage training leads at both layout thresholds. These unresolved issues limit the benefit of the documentation improvements.
